location_desc: Galápagos Tortoises live only on the Galápagos Islands, a remote archipelago in the Pacific Ocean belonging to Ecuador. Different species live on different islands, adapted to each island's unique environment — from lush highland forests to dry volcanic lowlands.
fun_facts: Galápagos Tortoises are the world's largest tortoises — they can weigh over 400 kg and live for more than 170 years!
Charles Darwin's observations of the different tortoise shapes on different islands helped inspire his theory of evolution.
The famous tortoise 'Lonesome George' was the last of his subspecies and died in 2012, making his subspecies extinct.
Galápagos Tortoises can go for up to a year without eating or drinking by slowly using stored fat and water.
When tortoises on flat islands stretch their necks to reach cacti, over time this led some populations to evolve longer necks and saddle-shaped shells.

translations.title: Galápagos Tortoise
translations.description: The Galápagos Tortoise is the world's largest tortoise and can live to be over 170 years old — some alive today may have been born before your great-great-great-grandparents! These slow, gentle giants live on the remote Galápagos Islands and helped inspire Charles Darwin's famous theory of evolution.

translations.title: Rùa Galápagos
translations.description: Rùa Galápagos là loài rùa cạn lớn nhất thế giới và có thể sống hơn 170 tuổi — một số con vẫn còn sống hôm nay có thể đã được sinh ra trước cả cụ cố của bạn! Những người khổng lồ chậm chạp và hiền lành này sống trên các đảo Galápagos xa xôi và đã giúp truyền cảm hứng cho lý thuyết tiến hóa nổi tiếng của Charles Darwin.
